# Implementation Plan: Dedicated Contact Page & Markdown Content Engine

**Branch**: `002-build-dedicated-contact` | **Date**: 2025-10-31 | **Spec**: `/specs/002-build-dedicated-contact/spec.md`  
**Input**: Feature specification from `/specs/002-build-dedicated-contact/spec.md`

**Note**: This template is generated by `/speckit.plan`. Every decision recorded here MUST reference the Nyan Cat Space constitution and demonstrate compliance before implementation begins.

## Summary

Ship a first-class contact experience and markdown-powered content system without breaking the cosmic terminal vibe. The new `contact.html` becomes the primary conversion surface: instead of a hosted form, it offers a frictionless email call-to-action (`mailto:`) plus copy-to-clipboard fallback and clear instructions, all honed for accessibility and reduced-motion preferences. In parallel, replace the Sanity integration with a local Markdown content engine: store project spotlights and blog posts under `content/`, transform them into HTML articles at runtime (or via pre-rendered snippets), and keep the portfolio entirely static with zero third-party dependencies. Target users include collaborators reaching out via email and readers exploring long-form write-ups; both flows must respect constitution gates for accessibility, performance, and narrative clarity.

## Technical Context

**Languages**: HTML5, Tailwind CSS utilities, vanilla JavaScript (ES2020)  
**Dependencies**: `styles/tailwind.css` (hand-authored utility set); no build tooling, frameworks, or external JS libraries; `mailto:` CTA with optional Clipboard API helper; Markdown parsing implemented via lightweight JS (custom parser or minimal library under 5 KB) or pre-rendered HTML fragments stored alongside Markdown.  
**Assets**: Media stored under `assets/`; individual files ≤ 200KB unless a variance is justified in Constitution Check  
**Validation**: Manual accessibility sweeps (keyboard navigation, contrast, reduced motion), responsive testing across mobile/desktop, email CTA smoke test (mailto launch + clipboard fallback), Markdown article rendering verification (JS enabled/disabled), optional automated linting if available  
**Target Platforms**: Evergreen desktop/mobile browsers, graceful fallback with JavaScript disabled  
**Performance Goals**: First meaningful paint < 2s on LTE, animation frame budgets ≤ 16ms, zero blocking network requests after initial page load; Markdown fetches should stay under 50 KB per article and reuse cached responses when possible.  
**Constraints**: Preserve retro terminal aesthetic, respect prefers-reduced-motion, stay fully static (no build tooling), maintain accessible content hierarchy, surface contact instructions that work with and without JavaScript, ensure Markdown content is readable without client-side parsing when possible  
**Scope**: Existing static pages plus new `contact.html`, `blog.html`, and `blog/post.html`, shared assets, Markdown parser module, and updated documentation for the local content workflow

## Constitution Check

*Gate: MUST pass before Phase 0 research. Re-validate after Phase 1 design.*

- **Terminal Fidelity**: Contact, projects, and blog pages reuse the black background + neon palette, monospace typography, and console blocks. Tailwind utilities may add CTA-specific styles while respecting the command-line aesthetic. Markdown-rendered articles must inherit the same headings, borders, and glow treatments to feel native to the terminal.
- **Cosmic Performance & Simplicity**: No hosted form submissions or external CMS calls. Markdown is parsed via lightweight JS (≤5 KB) or pre-rendered to static HTML snippets that can be swapped in without build tooling. Caching should minimize repeated fetches of Markdown files.
- **Universal Accessibility**: `contact.html` keeps the skip link target and explicit headings. CTA buttons expose visible focus rings, and clipboard confirmation uses `aria-live`. Markdown articles must render semantic HTML with proper heading levels, landmarks (`<main>`, `<article>`), and focus management for in-article links. When scripts are disabled, pre-rendered HTML ensures content stays readable.
- **Playful Animation Discipline**: Only subtle hover/focus pulses; no auto-running animations beyond existing starfield/Nyan Cat, which already observe reduced motion. Article load-ins rely on fades or static transitions that respect reduced motion.
- **Narrative & Content Clarity**: Navigation points to `contact.html`, `projects.html`, and `blog.html`, keeping story beats coherent. Contact hero copy references opening a “transmission,” while project/blog articles reinforce the cosmic hacker voice. Inline notes clarify how to browse articles and return to the index. Footer and skip link remain intact to preserve flow across breakpoints.

Inline `<template>` fallbacks mirror parsed output so static hosting works with or without JavaScript. Include `assets/ascii/contact-success.txt` if we need reusable console copy, ensuring assets directory organization remains clear.
